text:
Compound A contains 8.7% Hydrogen, 74% Carbon and 17.3% Nitrogen. The molecular formula of the compound is,

Given : Atomic masses of C, H and N are 12, 1 and 14 amu respectively.

The molar mass of the compound A is 162 g mol$^{-1}$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Mole ratio of H, C and N

$=\frac{8.7}{1}:\frac{74}{12}:\frac{17.3}{14}$

$=8.7:6.167:1.23$

$=\frac{8.7}{1.23}:\frac{6.167}{1.23}:\frac{1.23}{1.23}$

$=7:5:1$

$\therefore$ Emperical formula = $C_{5}H_{7}N$

$\therefore$ Molecular formula $=(C_{5}H_{7}N)_{n}$

Given molecular mass = 162

Molecular mass of $(C_{5}H_{7}N)_{n}$

$=(5\times 12+7\times 1+14)\times n$

$=(81)\times n$

$\therefore$ $81\times n=162$

$\Rightarrow n=2$

$\therefore$ Molecular formula $= C_{10}H_{14}N_{2}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th June Evening Shift

text:
Consider the following statements :

(A) The principal quantum number 'n' is a positive integer with values of 'n' = 1, 2, 3, ...

(B) The azimuthal quantum number 'l' for a given 'n' (principal quantum number) can have values as 'l' = 0, 1, 2, ...... n

(C) Magnetic orbital quantum number $'m_{l}'$ for a particular 'l' (azimuthal quantum number) has (2l + 1) values.

(D) $\pm$ 1/2 are the two possible orientations of electron spin.

(E) For l = 5, there will be a total of 9 orbital

Which of the above statements are correct?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
(A) Principal quantum number n is a positive integer and its possible values are n = 1, 2, 3 ........

$\therefore$ A is correct.

(B) Azimuthal quantum number 'l' for a given 'n' can have values as l = 0, 1, 2 ....... (n $-$ 1)

$\therefore$ Statement B is wrong.

(C) Magnetic orbital quantum number $m_{l}$ for particular l has values from $-$ l to + l including zero means 2l + 1 values.

$\therefore$ Statement C is correct.

(D) $\pm \quad \frac{1}{2}$ are the two possible orientation of electron spin.

$\therefore$ Statement D is correct.

(E) For l = 5, there will be a total of 11 orbitals.

$l$ = 0 $\Rightarrow$ s subshell

$l$ = 1 $\Rightarrow$ p subshell

$l$ = 2 $\Rightarrow$ d subshell

$l$ = 3 $\Rightarrow$ f subshell

$l$ = 4 $\Rightarrow$ g subshell

$l$ = 5 $\Rightarrow$ h subshell

We know,

Number of orbital in any subshell = 2$l$ + 1.

$\therefore$ For h subshell, number of orbitals = 2 $\times$ 5 + 1 = 11
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th June Evening Shift

text:
A student needs to prepare a buffer solution of propanoic acid and its sodium salt with pH 4. The ratio of $\frac{[CH_{3}CH_{2}COO^{-}]}{[CH_{3}CH_{2}COOH]}$ required to make buffer is $___________$.

Given : $K_{a}(CH_{3}CH_{2}COOH)=1.3\times 10^{-5}$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\mathrm{CH}_{3}\mathrm{CH}_{2}\mathrm{COOH}⇌\mathrm{CH}_{3}\mathrm{CH}_{2}\mathrm{COO}^{-}+\mathrm{H}^{+}$

From Henderson equation

$\mathrm{pH}=\mathrm{pK}_{\mathrm{a}}+\log \frac{\left [\mathrm{CH}_{3}\mathrm{CH}_{2}\mathrm{COO}^{-}\right ]}{[\mathrm{CH}_{3}\mathrm{CH}_{2}\mathrm{COOH}]}$

$4=-\log 1.3\times 10^{-5}+\log \frac{\left [\mathrm{CH}_{3}\mathrm{CH}_{2}\mathrm{COO}^{-}\right ]}{[\mathrm{CH}_{3}\mathrm{CH}_{2}\mathrm{COOH}]}$

$-\log 10^{-4}=-\log 1.3\times 10^{-5}+\log \frac{\left [\mathrm{CH}_{3}\mathrm{CH}_{2}\mathrm{COO}^{-}\right ]}{[\mathrm{CH}_{3}\mathrm{CH}_{2}\mathrm{COOH}]}$

$-\log 10^{-4}=-\log 1.3\times 10^{-5}\frac{[\mathrm{CH}_{3}\mathrm{CH}_{2}\mathrm{COOH}]}{\left [\mathrm{CH}_{3}\mathrm{CH}_{2}\mathrm{COO}^{-}\right ]}$

$10^{-4}=1.3\times 10^{-5}\frac{[\mathrm{CH}_{3}\mathrm{CH}_{2}\mathrm{COOH}]}{\left [\mathrm{CH}_{3}\mathrm{CH}_{2}\mathrm{COO}^{-}\right ]}$

$\frac{\left [\mathrm{CH}_{3}\mathrm{CH}_{2}\mathrm{COO}^{-}\right ]}{[\mathrm{CH}_{3}\mathrm{CH}_{2}\mathrm{COOH}]}=0.13$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th June Evening Shift

text:
For combustion of one mole of magnesium in an open container at 300 K and 1 bar pressure, $\Delta_{C}H^{$\Theta} = $-$601.70 kJ mol$^{-1}$, the magnitude of change in internal energy for the reaction is $__________ kJ. ($Nearest integer)

(Given : $R = 8.3 J K^{-1}$ mol$^{-1})$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\mathrm{Mg}(\mathrm{s})+\frac{1}{2}\mathrm{O}_{2}(\mathrm{g})⟶\mathrm{MgO}(\mathrm{s})$

$\begin{array}{l} \Delta \mathrm{H}=\Delta \mathrm{U}+\Delta \mathrm{ngRT} \\  \\ \Delta \mathrm{ng}=-\dfrac{1}{2} \\  \\ -601.70=\Delta \mathrm{U}-\dfrac{1}{2}(8.3)(300)\times 10^{-3} \\  \\ \Delta \mathrm{U}=-601.70+1.245 \\  \\ \Delta \mathrm{U}\simeq -600\mathrm{kJ} \end{array}$

The magnitude of change in internal energy is $600\mathrm{kJ}$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th June Evening Shift

text:
For the given reactions

$Sn^{2+} + 2e^{-}$ $\to$ Sn

$Sn^{4+} + 4e^{-}$ $\to$ Sn

the electrode potentials are ; $E_{Sn^{2+}/Sn}^{o}=-0.140$ V and $E_{Sn^{4+}/Sn}^{o}=+0.010$ V. The magnitude of standard electrode potential for $Sn^{4+}/Sn^{2+}$ i.e. $E_{Sn^{4+}/Sn^{2+}}^{o}$ is $_____________$ $\times$ $10^{-2} V. ($Nearest integer)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\mathrm{Sn}⟶\mathrm{Sn}^{2+}+2\mathrm{e}^{-}\mathrm{E}_{1}^{0}=0.140\mathrm{V}$

$\mathrm{Sn}^{4+}+4\mathrm{e}^{-}⟶\mathrm{Sn}\mathrm{E}_{2}^{0}=0.010\mathrm{V}$

$\begin{array}{l} \mathrm{Sn}^{4+}+2\mathrm{e}^{-}⟶\mathrm{Sn}^{2+}\mathrm{E}_{\text{cell}}^{0} \\  \\ \mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{cell}}^{\mathrm{O}}=\dfrac{\mathrm{n}_{2}\mathrm{E}_{2}^{\mathrm{o}}+\mathrm{n}_{1}\mathrm{E}_{1}^{0}}{\mathrm{n}}=\dfrac{4(0.010)+2(0.140)}{2} \\  \\ \mathrm{E}_{\text{cell}}^{0}=0.16\mathrm{V}=16\times 10^{-2}\mathrm{V} \end{array}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th June Evening Shift

text:
(a) CoCl$_{3}.4NH_{3},    (b)$ CoCl$_{3}.5NH_{3},      (c)$ CoCl$_{3}.6NH_{3}$    and    (d) CoCl$(NO_{3})_{2}.5NH_{3}$.

Number of complex(es) which will exist in cis-trans form is/are $_______________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
(a) $\mathrm{CoCl}{}_{3}\cdot 4\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}$ is $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}){}_{4}\mathrm{Cl}{}_{2}]\mathrm{Cl}$, an octahedral $\mathrm{MA}{}_{4}\mathrm{B}{}_{2}$ complex: the two $\mathrm{Cl}{}^{-}$ ligands can be adjacent (cis) or opposite (trans), so it exists in cis-trans forms.

(b) $\mathrm{CoCl}{}_{3}\cdot 5\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}$ is $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}){}_{5}\mathrm{Cl}]\mathrm{Cl}{}_{2}$, an $\mathrm{MA}{}_{5}\mathrm{B}$ complex with only one arrangement.

(c) $\mathrm{CoCl}{}_{3}\cdot 6\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}$ is $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}){}_{6}]\mathrm{Cl}{}_{3}$, an $\mathrm{MA}{}_{6}$ complex with no geometrical isomers.

(d) $\mathrm{CoCl}(\mathrm{NO}{}_{3}){}_{2}\cdot 5\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}$ is $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}){}_{5}\mathrm{Cl}](\mathrm{NO}{}_{3}){}_{2}$ (or its ionisation isomer $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}){}_{5}(\mathrm{NO}{}_{3})]\mathrm{Cl}(\mathrm{NO}{}_{3})$); either way the complex ion is $\mathrm{MA}{}_{5}\mathrm{B}$ and has no cis-trans forms.

Only complex (a) exists in cis-trans form.

Hence, the answer is 1.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th June Evening Shift

text: The complete combustion of 0.492 g of an organic compound containing 'C', 'H' and 'O' gives 0.793 g of $CO_{2}$ and 0.442 g of $H_{2}O$. The percentage of oxygen composition in the organic compound is $______________. ($nearest integer)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Total organic compound = 0.492 gm

Produced $CO_{2} = 0.793 gm$

$\therefore$ Moles of $CO_{2} =$ $\frac{0.793}{44}$

$\therefore$ Moles of C atoms = $\frac{0.793}{44}$

$\therefore$ Weight of C atoms = $\frac{0.793}{44}$ $\times$ 12 = 0.216 g

Produced $H_{2}O = 0.442 gm$

$\therefore$ Moles of $H_{2}O =$ $\frac{0.442}{18}$

$\therefore$ Moles of H atoms = $\frac{0.442}{18}\times 2$

$\therefore$ Weight of H atoms = $\frac{0.442}{18}$ $\times$ 2 = 0.05 g

$\therefore$ Weight of O atoms

= 0.492 $-$ (0.216 + 0.05)

= 0.226 gm

% by mass of oxygen in compound

= $\frac{0.226}{0.492}$ $\times$ 100 = 46%
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th June Evening Shift

text: 0.01 M KMnO$_{4}$ solution was added to 20.0 mL of 0.05 M Mohr's salt solution through a burette. The initial reading of 50 mL burette is zero. The volume of KMnO$_{4}$ solution left in the burette after the end point is $_____________ mL. ($nearest integer)

solution.body:
Meq of oxidizing agent $=$ Meq of reducing agent

$\left (\mathrm{M}\times \mathrm{V}\times \mathrm{n}_{\text{F}}\right )_{\mathrm{KMnO}_{4}}=\left (\mathrm{M}\times \mathrm{V}\times \mathrm{n}_{\text{F}}\right )_{\text{Mohr’s salt}}$

$0.01\times V\times 5=0.05\times 20\times 1$

Volume required $=20\mathrm{ml}$

Since initial volume of $\mathrm{KMnO}_{4}$ in burette is $50\mathrm{ml}$.

Hence volume of $\mathrm{KMnO}_{4}$ left in the burette after end point is $30\mathrm{ml}$.
